candidate_ledger.continuation_case: Energy equities can extend if crude strength persists and the EIA report reinforces tight or improving petroleum balances.

candidate_ledger.continuation_case: Cash-like Treasury bills should deliver small positive carry with very low volatility if risk assets remain weak.
evidence: SHORT_TREASURY return_3s was 0.04% and active return_5s was 1.60% because SPY declined.
Three-month Treasury yield was 3.85% on July 17.
Volatility_21s was 0.25% and max drawdown_21s was -0.01%.
candidate_ledger.invalidation_condition: Risk assets rally strongly enough that capital-preservation exposure is no longer competitive with SPY.
candidate_ledger.reversal_case: Because expected one-week carry is small, any SPY rebound would make this exposure lag equities materially.
candidate_ledger.time_window_catalyst: No specific catalyst beyond short-term Treasury carry over the scoring week.

key_risks: A broad risk-on rebound led by technology and growth causes SPY to outperform the selected value/defensive mix.
Treasury yields rise despite soft CPI/PPI, pressuring real estate and other rate-sensitive equities.
Oil reverses sharply after the recent surge or the EIA petroleum report disappoints energy bulls.
The recent relative-strength signals reverse because one-week price moves were short-covering rather than durable rotation.

portfolio_rationale: The portfolio avoids recent high-beta growth underperformance and diversifies across value, financials, rate-sensitive real estate, healthcare, and energy. All selected holdings have base forecasts above the SPY base forecast, with no non-SPY cluster above the 50% cap.
rationale_summary: Base case is continued one-week rotation away from mega-cap growth toward value, defensive, financial, and selected commodity-linked exposures. Energy is included at a limited weight because it has a clear scheduled catalyst but elevated reversal risk after a sharp move.
